title: Program
definition: A program is a finite representation of instructions and data intended to produce defined behavior when executed by a compatible computing system.
purpose: Separate a program representation from an informal wish and from the running process that executes it.
history: Stored-program computing made instructions representable data; this record keeps only the technology-neutral curriculum boundary.
mental_model: A program is an inspectable instruction-and-data contract waiting for a compatible execution environment.
analogy: A written score can guide a performance, but the score is not the performance and cannot act without performers and an environment.
real_world_usage: Distinguishing source artifacts from running behavior
Explaining why compatibility and execution environment matter
common_mistakes: Calling any vague goal a program
Treating the program file as the running process
industry_notes: Repositories, builds, deployments, and processes must preserve which program representation is being executed.
ai_notes: AI-generated text becomes a program only when it forms a valid representation whose behavior can be executed and verified.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to distinguish a program, source representation, process, and output.
exercise_candidates: Classify examples as program, running process, input, or output
lab_candidates: Represent a small everyday procedure as explicit instructions and data
project_candidates: Define the instruction set for a tiny simulator
